title: The G42 License: What the Commerce Department Announced and What It Didn't Disclose About Trump's Crypto Firm
body:
On July 10, 2026, the US Commerce Department announced a policy change granting the United Arab Emirates — specifically UAE companies including G42 — license-free access to advanced US AI chips and technology. The announcement was made by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. The public rationale, as stated in the Commerce Department release, was partly based on "the UAE's status as a U.S. Major Defense Partner and its support in advancing U.S. national security interests," including assistance during the Iran war.

The same day, The Independent and The New York Times reported that four days before President Trump's January 2026 inauguration, a UAE royal-backed company — MGX, chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE's national security adviser — spent $500 million to acquire a 49 percent stake in World Liberty Financial, the Trump family cryptocurrency firm. The deal was initially kept secret; $187 million flowed immediately to Trump entities. Financial disclosures later showed Trump personally made more than $1 billion in 2025 from the family crypto companies.

A G42 employee held a job at World Liberty Financial while the 2025 G42-World Liberty deal was being negotiated, the New York Times reported. G42 is chaired by the same Sheikh Tahnoon whose MGX investment vehicle made the World Liberty purchase. All sides have denied any conflict of interest.

Separately, in 2022, US intelligence agencies obtained information that the UAE, through G42, had transferred technology to Huawei that enabled China to extend the range of its air-to-air missiles, the Financial Times reported. G42 called that reporting "false and defamatory" at the time and reportedly cut ties with Huawei as part of a 2024 Microsoft investment deal.

Senator Elizabeth Warren called the Commerce Department policy change "a corrupt deal" and called on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler to testify before Congress. Former Biden administration official Chris McGuire wrote on X: "This is a HUGE deal, poses massive national security risks, will slow the US AI buildout, and will cause the largest data centers in the world to be built in the UAE instead of the US."

The Commerce Department announcement is a US government action with national security implications. The MGX investment is a documented financial transaction with Trump family entities. The G42 employee staffing overlap during negotiations is a documented fact reported by the New York Times. The 2022 Huawei-to-China missile technology transfer is documented in US intelligence findings reported by the Financial Times.

The national security justification (UAE defense partnership, Iran war assistance) and the financial relationship (MGX / Trump crypto / $187M immediate payment / $1B annual Trump crypto income) exist on different disclosure tracks. The Commerce Department announcement does not mention the latter; it cites only the former. The story is the gap between what the US government said its decision was based on — and what its own public record shows about the financial relationships of the person whose company just received the policy benefit.

The Commerce Department's stated rationale — defense partnership, regional assistance — does not engage with the specific competing facts in the public record. Sheikh Tahnoon's MGX vehicle made the $500M World Liberty purchase four days before inauguration; G42 now receives license-free AI chip access; the same G42 was flagged by US intelligence in 2022 for enabling Chinese weapons development. None of this appears in the policy announcement.
verdict: The Commerce Department's announcement cited national security interests as the basis for granting UAE companies license-free AI chip access. The public record provides a competing data point that the announcement did not disclose: Sheikh Tahnoon's MGX had four days earlier invested $500M in Trump's family cryptocurrency firm, and G42 was previously flagged by US intelligence for enabling Chinese missile technology. The disclosure gap — not the policy itself — is the story.

documents_absent: Commerce Department disclosure of MGX World Liberty financial relationship in policy announcement
Commerce Department disclosure of 2022 FT Huawei intelligence finding in policy announcement
